primitives.name: Gate Latch Interaction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Besides this, moreover, the gate is fastened on the garden-side by a string nailed to the gate-post Here, as often as one wished, could the following sight be observed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'latch state (dimensionless: 0 = latched, 1 = unlatched)', 'S': 'string tension (N)', 'F': 'force applied by snout (N)'}
primitives.assumptions: Gate mechanism operates under static equilibrium; string tension is sufficient to hold latch in place until force exceeds threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F > T_threshold, L transitions from 0 to 1.

layer2.mapping: State transition function models how mechanical action (snout force) alters physical constraint (latch state).
layer2.telemetry: Observation of gate opening event frequency and associated snout-force magnitude.

primitives.name: Bark-Induced Gate Opening
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the barking came from the garden, he opened the gate to get inside.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'bark intensity (dimensionless)', 'G': 'gate response (boolean: 0 = closed, 1 = open)', 'T': 'time since last bark (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Dogs associate barks with potential presence of another dog inside; conditional probability P(G=1|B>threshold) increases with temporal proximity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B(t) > B_threshold and T < T_max, G(t+1) = 1.

layer2.mapping: Behavioral pattern mirrors conditional inference in probabilistic logic: P(gate_open | bark_in_garden) = f(bark_intensity, time_since_bark).
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of gate openings correlated with bark detection events.

primitives.name: Nose Force Transduction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Now it fell out that once, while making the attempt, he raised his nose higher than usual and hit the latch from below so as to lift it off its hook, and the gate unclosed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_n': 'nose force vector (N)', 'd': 'displacement of latch (m)', 'k': 'spring constant of latch mechanism (N/m)'}
primitives.assumptions: Mechanical system follows Hooke's law; successful unlocking requires F_n * d > E_unlock_threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F_n · d ≥ k·Δx, latch disengages.

layer2.mapping: Sensorimotor integration model where proprioceptive feedback guides motor output to achieve mechanical goal.
layer2.telemetry: Measurement of nose displacement during gate manipulation attempts.

The resulting mechanical interaction—leveraging string tension and lever arm geometry—opens the gate. This process reflects a dualistic learning loop: sensory input (bark) leads to motor output (nose force), which modifies environmental state (gate open). The system exhibits emergent properties such as memory retention (repetition after success) and adaptation (changing strategy upon constraint change). Failure modes include insufficient force application or misalignment of snout trajectory. These behaviors can be modeled as stochastic processes governed by reward-based reinforcement learning principles, where each successful outcome reinforces the behavioral sequence. The interplay between two agents (dogs) introduces a multi-agent dynamic, wherein one dog acts as teacher and the other as learner, creating a hierarchical structure of knowledge transfer.
